rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for someone who is lazy or avoids doing work.

example.english: They always say they’ll do it tomorrow, so they are really indolent.
example.traditional: 佢成日話聽日先做，真係好懶。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 waa6 ting1 jat6 sin1 zou6 zan1 hai6 hou2 laan5

rows.note: Use this for a more explicit description of habitual laziness, especially in careful or written contexts.

example.english: They have been criticized since childhood for being indolent and lacking perseverance.
example.traditional: 佢自細就被人批評懶惰，做事冇恆心。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zi6 sai3 zau6 bei6 jan4 pai1 ping4 laan5 do6 zou6 si6 mou5 hang4 sam1

rows.note: Use this when the person is habitually slack, idle, or lacking energy and discipline rather than simply unwilling to do one task.

example.english: On holidays, I become so indolent that I do not even want to leave the house.
example.traditional: 放假成個人懶散落嚟，連門口都唔想出。
example.jyutping: fong3 gaa3 seng4 go3 jan4 laan5 saan2 lok6 lai4 lin4 mun4 hau2 dou1 m4 soeng2 ceot1
